label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, secret-rotation, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 7 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy webhook-receiver: WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION v2 -> v1); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: secret-rotation
case.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the webhook receiver with a rotated secret the provider does not sign with (WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, while the provider signs with v1): every webhook fails its signature check and is refused with a 400, so no event reaches Kafka, and the provider keeps sending them again, with backoff.
case.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

fault.name: secret-rotation
fault.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook
fault.cause: a deploy of the webhook receiver with a rotated secret the provider does not sign with (WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, while the provider signs with v1): every webhook fails its signature check and is refused with a 400, so no event reaches Kafka, and the provider keeps sending them again, with backoff
expected_symptoms: the books cannot catch up with the provider: the money check cannot settle, the provider's webhooks not acknowledged, and the books rule fires at its second evaluation, about 50 s after the deploy
the receiver refuses every webhook with a 400, counts it as bad_signature and logs 'webhook refused: bad signature'; the provider sends its growing backlog again and again, tens of times a second
nothing new is booked or confirmed, and both consumers' lag stays at 0: nothing reaches Kafka

payments and refunds still go through, but one whose answer was lost cannot be confirmed: its client's retries get 503 again, so the 5xx share of POST /payments about doubles and its p95 climbs to about 0.6 s, both under their thresholds

after the rollback the books catch up within about three minutes: the provider sends each refused webhook again within a minute of its last try, and one whose acknowledgement is then lost (the traffic's noise) a minute later
fault.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, 186 of the provider's webhooks up to it had not been acknowledged yet.

diagnosis.hypothesis: At 19:11:49 webhook-receiver was redeployed with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. The provider still signs its webhooks with the secret the receiver used before, so every incoming webhook now fails signature verification. The receiver rejects each one as bad_signature and does not acknowledge it, and nothing new reaches provider-events. The provider keeps resending unacknowledged webhooks, so incoming traffic climbs steeply: about 26/s by 19:13, all of it bad_signature. Because the backlog of unacknowledged webhooks only grows (186 at the alert), the money check cannot settle up to its cutoff, and BooksBehindProvider fires. The consumers, Kafka and the database look healthy; the break is at the receiver's signature check.

evidence.shows: All containers are running and healthy. webhook-receiver alone was restarted later, at 19:11:50, after the rest of the stack started around 19:10:22-30.
The newest deploy is webhook-receiver at 19:11:49 with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. No other service changed after startup.
The total webhook receive rate rises sharply after 19:11:49, from about 3.7/s to about 25/s. This fits the provider resending webhooks that were not acknowledged.

Before 19:11:53 every webhook was queued. After the deploy, the bad_signature series appears and grows to about 26/s, while queued falls toward zero (1.46/s at 19:12:23, then no further points). Every webhook is now rejected at the signature check.
The receiver logged no WARN or ERROR lines, so the signature rejections are not logged at warning level. The metrics are the only place they show.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to the settings it had before the 19:11:49 deploy, i.e. the previous WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION, so it again verifies with the secret the provider actually signs with. The provider will then redeliver the backlog of unacknowledged webhooks, the receiver will queue them, and the consumers will catch up. Afterwards, run money_check with wait=true to confirm the books settle. Re-attempt the v2 rotation only in step with the provider, for example by accepting both secrets during the rotation.

diagnosis.blast_radius: webhook-receiver is recreated, so it pauses briefly during the restart. The provider keeps resending during that pause, so no webhooks are lost. When the receiver comes back, the redelivered backlog causes a burst of events on provider-events. The ledger-consumer runs in idempotent mode, and the confirmer matches events by our id, so redeliveries should not double-book. Not yet verified: whether some events were queued under v2 but still fail later. If v2 was meant to be the provider's new secret, the rollback could break verification again.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes signature failures worse, redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, then coordinate the correct secret with the provider side. Watch klaxon_webhooks_received_total by result: after the rollback, queued should rise and bad_signature should drop to zero.
